title: Third-Order Affine Replacement Bound
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,U,V\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$, with $(A,D)$ measurable up to null sets and $D,U,V\in L^3(\mu)$. Suppose $U$ and $V$ have equal means and equal second moments, and each is independent of $(A,D)$. Let $\psi\in C^3(\mathbb R)$, and suppose $|\psi^{(3)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. If $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable, then
\[\left|\mathbb E\psi(A+DU)-\mathbb E\psi(A+DV)\right|\le \frac C6\left(\mathbb E|U|^3+\mathbb E|V|^3\right)\mathbb E|D|^3.\]
hypotheses_covered: $(A,D)$ is measurable up to null sets
